# The `DAGTypeLegalizer` Class Reference

## Description {#details}

<p>This takes an arbitrary <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/selectiondag">SelectionDAG</a> as input and hacks on it until only value types the target machine can handle are left.</p>


<p>This involves promoting small sizes to large sizes or splitting up large values into small values.</p>


<p>Definition at line 31 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/codegen/lib/codegen/selectiondag/legalizetypes-h">LegalizeTypes.h</a>.</p>

<p>This performs an expansion of the integer result for a fixed point multiplication.</p>


<p>The default expansion performs rounding down towards negative infinity, though targets that do care about rounding should specify a target hook for rounding and provide their own expansion or lowering of fixed point multiplication to be consistent with rounding.</p>

<p>Given a processed operand <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> which was promoted to a larger integer type, this returns the promoted value.</p>


<p>The low bits of the promoted value corresponding to the original type are exactly equal to <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a>. The extra bits contain rubbish, so the promoted value may need to be zero- or sign-extended from the original type before it is usable (the helpers SExtPromotedInteger and ZExtPromotedInteger can do this for you). For example, if <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> is an i16 and was promoted to an i32, then this method returns an i32, the lower 16 bits of which coincide with <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a>, and the upper 16 bits of which contain rubbish.</p>

<p>Given a processed vector <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> which was split into vectors of half the size, this method returns the halves.</p>


<p>The first elements of <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> coincide with the elements of Lo; the remaining elements of <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> coincide with the elements of Hi: <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> is what you would get by concatenating Lo and Hi. For example, if <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> is a v8i32 that was split into two v4i32's, then this method returns the two v4i32's, with Lo corresponding to the first 4 elements of <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a>, and Hi to the last 4 elements.</p>
